evals.prompt: A browser automation call reports that it dragged the volume slider successfully. No post-action value or visual state was observed.
The player rises after jump input, but one second later falls through the floor. Determine the jump verification result.
While verifying a Save button, the same already-acquired screen clearly shows the required navigation title clipped. Save itself works.
A setting changes successfully and reopening the same settings panel is cheap. The requirement includes persistence.
A native desktop workflow must be tested, but the current environment cannot launch or interact with the application. Static code inspection looks correct.
Runtime verification finds that HP UI does not update. The project already provides a project index, system map, integration trace, and implementation anchors.
A pure internal parsing helper was refactored with unchanged contract and focused deterministic tests.
A menu button is required to start a game. Calling the scene-loading function directly succeeds, but the menu was never exercised.
A material UI workflow is VERIFIED with before and settled-after screenshots. No independent review is currently required.
The project already has a canonical Evidence/acceptance artifact store for runtime evidence.
A small project has no persistent evidence store. A material runtime check produces screenshots in the current session/artifact workspace.
Runtime logs report that the new start screen loaded successfully. A current screenshot from the same run shows the screen is visibly distorted: controls overlap and the layout is misaligned.

A current screenshot was captured to verify one Start button. The same screenshot also clearly shows clipped navigation, wrong spacing, and a missing required logo on the accepted start-screen surface.

A trustworthy current screenshot already proves the unchanged start-screen layout and logo placement. The agent now needs to cite those same unchanged visible facts again before any relevant visual/state change occurred.
After screenshot A was captured, the agent changes the start-screen container/layout. It wants to use screenshot A as proof that the new layout is correct.
A screenshot shows a Settings button rendered correctly. No click or resulting navigation state was exercised, but the claim is that the button works and opens Settings.
The approved surface authority places the primary Start action centered below the title. The rendered button has exactly the correct color, typography, radius, and label but appears in a side panel.
Every required start-screen component exists and is individually styled correctly, but the current screenshot materially contradicts the approved hierarchy and layout composition.
A visual authority contains exact spacing/color constraints plus prose/reference guidance describing the intended hierarchy and composition.
The authority specifies relative placement and hierarchy but no exact x/y coordinates. The rendered surface visibly matches that relative structure.
The agent's generated HTML Working Atlas places Settings above Start, but the canonical project surface authority places Settings below Start.

A live game is demonstrably continuing to animate, but a screenshot tool reports successful new captures whose image content remains byte-identical across several seconds. The latest file has a fresh timestamp and looks plausible. The agent wants to use it as proof of the current rendered state.

expected.acceptable_method: independent ongoing activity or controlled observable stimulus

evals.prompt: A legitimately static settings screen produces two byte-identical screenshots one second apart. No independent signal or controlled stimulus says the screen should have changed.
